edges.notes: createUser: axiosInstance.post(Routes.API.USERS, user) on the one axios.create() instance (lib-client/react-query/axios.ts, no baseURL, so root-relative on the same Next app); Routes.API.USERS = '/api/users/' (lib-client/constants.ts; trailing slash because next.config.js sets trailingSlash: true, no trailing slash in the route spelling). pages/api/users/index.ts is a next-connect handler (apiHandler() = nc(ncOptions), onNoMatch answers 405), so its methods are the handler.get/handler.post registrations; the route line is that handler.post call

getUser(id): axiosInstance.get(`${Routes.API.USERS}${id}`) = /api/users/<id>; the id parameter fills a later hole, not the path's leading part, so the label stays at this call. pages/api/users/profile.ts is the only static sibling, and a session id is a cuid, never 'profile'
createPost: axiosInstance.post(Routes.API.POSTS, post), Routes.API.POSTS = '/api/posts/'; next-connect handler.post
getPosts(params): axiosInstance.get(Routes.API.POSTS, { params }), params only fill the query; called twice in usePosts (query and next-page prefetch), one request expression
updatePost({ id, post }): axiosInstance.patch(`${Routes.API.POSTS}${id}`, post); next-connect handler.patch
createSeed: axiosInstance.post(Routes.API.SEED), Routes.API.SEED = '/api/seed/'; the seed handler registers handler.post and handler.get

getImage(imageUrl) is an exported helper whose request (axiosInstance.get(imageUrl, { responseType: 'blob' }), line 11) takes the whole URL as a parameter, so the label is at its one call, here. imageUrl is getAvatarPath(user) (user.image when it is a full URL, a runtime value on any host, else `/uploads/avatars/${…}`) or getHeaderImagePath(user) (`/uploads/headers/${…}`), lib-client/imageLoaders.ts. /uploads/* is served by the custom server's server.use('/uploads', express.static(…)) (server/index.ts:16), static files, not a route; no pages/ or pages/api/ file serves /uploads. So the request reaches no route in the repo
updateUser({ id, … }): axiosInstance.patch(`${Routes.API.USERS}${id}`, formData, config); next-connect handler.patch (multer middleware first)

getUser(params): axiosInstance.get(Routes.API.PROFILE, { params }), Routes.API.PROFILE = '/api/users/profile/'. Both pages/api/users/profile.ts and pages/api/users/[id].ts could match; Next.js dispatches a static segment before a dynamic one, so profile.ts
getUsers(params): axiosInstance.get(Routes.API.USERS, { params }), params only fill the query; next-connect handler.get
